evidence: R2 sets window_living.position := open at 10:00 | R6 sets window_living.position := closed when ac_living.mode == cool | Both rules control the same device state (window_living.position) with opposite values | R2 has no condition checking the AC mode, so it can run while the AC is cooling | window_living open increases temp_living (hot outdoor air in summer), which works against the AC's cooling

explanation: R2 starts watering every day at 06:00, which raises soil moisture. Once moisture goes above 60%, R4 stops the watering, so each rule's effect sets off the other. R2 doesn't check soil moisture, so it also waters soil that is already wet, and R4 may never fire because moisture never crosses 60%. R4 also turns off only 'watering' and leaves 'flow' on, so the controller is left half-stopped.

repair: Add the condition 'soil_moisture <= 60' to R2 so it does not start watering soil that is already wet, and have R4 also set irrigation.flow := off when it stops watering.

If that's a concern, you could add rules that turn each device off once the room is back between 20 and 24 °C.
